diagnostics.notes: Both claims verified against their own abstracts. Side A: 'LDL (r = 0.30, P = 0.001)' within the correlation results for patients with type-2 DM; extraction of exposure (serum adiponectin), outcome (LDL), direction (+), and estimate are correct. Side B: 'Adiponectin levels were negatively associated with waist circumference, waist-hip ratio, PTX-3 and LDL'; extraction of direction (-) is correct. Comparability holds: both are cross-sectional correlation analyses of circulating adiponectin versus LDL, unadjusted, with the same index/reference orientation (higher adiponectin vs LDL level). The findings are genuinely opposite in direction. A text-supported contextual difference exists: A was conducted exclusively in patients with type-2 DM and explicitly reports a significant interaction between adiponectin and metabolic syndrome status in relation to lipid profile (with the adiponectin-LDL correlation strengthening as MetS components increase), whereas B studied a mixed cohort of MetS patients and non-MetS controls with no reported diabetes status. This population difference is concrete and could explain the opposite directions, so apparent_contradiction is used rather than contradictory.

source_evidence.quote: Adiponectin was negatively correlated with waist circumference (r = -0.16, P = 0.06) and positively with HbA1c (r = 0.19, P = 0.032), total cholesterol (r = 0.23, P = 0.017), LDL (r = 0.30, P = 0.001), SD-LDL (r = 0.41, P < 0.001), and SD-LDL/LDL (r = 0.22, P = 0.023).
Significant interaction was observed between adiponectin and metabolic syndrome in relation to serum lipid profile.
A single center cross-sectional study was conducted on 173 patients with type-2 DM (82 males and 91 females).
Adiponectin levels were negatively associated with waist circumference, waist-hip ratio, PTX-3 and LDL.

In 180 individuals, including controls and patients with MetS, we measured fasting plasma insulin, high sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), pentraxin-3 (PTX-3), interleukin-33 (IL-33), irisin, RBP-4, and adiponectin using ELISA kits.

verdict.label: apparent_contradiction
verdict.rationale: Both claims are correctly extracted. The same association (circulating adiponectin vs LDL, unadjusted correlation) is reported with opposite directions: side A found a positive correlation in 173 patients with type-2 DM (r = 0.30, P = 0.001), while side B found adiponectin negatively associated with LDL in a cohort of 180 MetS patients and controls. This is a genuine directional contradiction with sufficient comparability. A supported contextual difference could explain it: side A's population is exclusively type-2 DM patients and its abstract explicitly reports a significant interaction between adiponectin and metabolic syndrome status in relation to lipid profile (the adiponectin-LDL correlation varying with the number of MetS components), whereas side B studied a mixed MetS/controls population with diabetes status not reported. The differing study populations therefore provide a concrete, text-supported explanation for the opposite findings.
